rv.q: Instead, Frecknall revivifies Streetcar as a true ensemble piece — a haunting jazz symphony with a devastating trio at its center.

Streetcar has the additional depth and richness of Williams at his best; one of the standout aspects of this production—thanks again to the actors’ and Frecknall’s care—is the breadth of Williams’ language; its vibrancy and perfectly aimed poison darts of lyricism hit mark after mark.
There's little poignancy in the performance.
